questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Toulouse since I have an interest in learning French and the climate is quite nice for the most part.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very challenging semester academically with a lot of lectures and classes. Other than that I had a good time.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of it was sent to you by email, albeit always a bit later than you'd like.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction week where we were given some information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult since I was only staying in Toulouse for four months and most landlords want renters to stay for at least one year. Ended up finding an apartment through Airbnb and making a deal directly with the landlord to avoid paying large Airbnb fees.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it's completely fine to live off campus since the city is easy to get around with a bike or them metro if your apartment is near a metrostation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university offers dormitory accommodation through the organisation called CROUS which is seemingly allocated at random. You'll have to find accommodation yourself if you didn't get an offer to stay at CROUS.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Fairly confusing. Some courses were "limited seats" meaning that they were firstly allocated to the people that "needed" to take the course and thereafter based on your grades. It wasn't really clear whether you were registered for a course until later during the semester, so you'd just show up anyway which wasn't a problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could send an email to the Toulouse School of Economics "Mobility and International Relations Officer" Geneviève Doumeng or show up at her office in person to ask her questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There weren't a lot of flexibility on which courses to choose since you need 30 ECTS and there aren't that many to choose between when you don't understand French. I wanted to register for 1 limited seat course but didn't get a seat unfortunately.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Since KU doesn't have a partnership with TSM (Toulouse School of Management) I was told I couldn't take any classes there. It seemed like if you talked to Geneviève you could perhaps figure something out. Since the courses at TSE was very demanding (had 10 different courses too), and TSM's courses less so, I would suggest trying to register for courses at TSM to reduce the amount of work you have.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to take a lot of courses (10) to get 30 ECTS and in some of the courses the workload was quite big relative to the amount of ECTS the course was worth. I spent more time on studying than I do at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lectures and classes than at KU. You don't get to solve a lot of problems in class, instead the TA goes through the problem set and you can try to solve it on your own either before or after class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
5 point courses:
Macroeconomics
Game Theory
Intermediate Econometrics

2,5 point courses:
Theory of Incentives
R programming

2 point courses:
Understanding real world organisations
Evolution of economic behaviour
Project management
Markov chains and applications
Probability modelling

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Project management, Understanding real world organisations and Evolution of economic behaviour simply because the workload was less than the other courses. I would also recommend to stay away from Intermediate Econometrics unless you're already very good at econometrics. It's in my opinion the most difficult course I have ever taken.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None I think

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was very cheap. I almost exclusively got around by using the vélôToulouse bikes which has an annual subscription fee for 20 euros. Public transportation is also very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sports was placed in the afternoon where we had lectures

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of different sports (if your timetable allows for it) and parties organised by the TSE student organisation called BDE.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to a BDE party I guess. Drinking at la Garonne is obligatory as an Erasmus student.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a day trip to one of the cities near Toulouse, or to the Pyrenees perhaps.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Didn't notice any major culture differences that I needed to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Biggest problem was a language barrier since my French isn't great and not everyone speaks English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sitting down for a coffee and a pastry most days

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Avoid Intermediate Econometrics, try to take courses at TSM and finally ask yourself if you're up for the challenge or perhaps should consider going on exchange at a different university to have a more relaxed semester

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think Toulouse is a great city to go on exchange in, however TSE is an academically tough institution in my opinion. Therefore I would say there are pros and cons to going on exchange in Toulouse as an economics student.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends with other exchange students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Passing all my courses, specifically Intermediate Econometrics (I didn't)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
